free_tier.stated: 5 GB stored on Spark (no-cost) plan; 1 GB downloaded per day; 50k download ops/day
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: 1 GB/day download (~30 GB/month) free, then $0.12/GB; outbound networking 5 GB/month. The 1 GB/DAY download cap is the binding constraint, not the 5 GB stored.

tooling: Firebase SDKs (web/Android/iOS), Admin SDK, gsutil/gcloud storage against the underlying GCS bucket, `firebase storage:upload`; rclone can hit the bucket with GCS (not rclone's 'firebase'. That is the Realtime DB). Public download URLs via `getDownloadURL` / Firebase download tokens.
chaining: 5 GB per PROJECT. Projects per Google account on Spark are limited to 'a small number of projects (usually around 5-10)'. So ~25-50 GB/account, not a big multiplier. Multiple Google accounts is the only axis. Deleting a project takes 30 days and still counts against quota, which badly hurts churn-and-burn cycling.
limits_note: 1 GB/day egress (~30 GB/mo) is the practical ceiling. A 5 GB store is refetchable only 6x/month. Download-op cap 50k/day. Spark also caps Cloud Storage at 5 GB-months and 100 GB/month downloaded for the *default* bucket variant. No billing = hard stop, not overage.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Hard daily reset at midnight; exceeding it fails requests until reset. Project deletion is 30 days and blocked from quota reuse, so account cycling is slow.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.
